question: _____ recorded the highest population density in 2011, as per the 2011 Census of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**North East Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **2011 Census of India**, North East Delhi recorded the **highest population density** in the country.
 
• North East Delhi had a population density of **37,346 persons per square kilometer**, making it the most densely populated district in India.
 
• Population density is calculated as the number of persons per square kilometer of land area.
 
• North East Delhi is part of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi, which is itself one of the most urbanized and densely populated regions in India.
 
• The high population density in this region is attributed to urbanization, migration, and the concentration of residential settlements in limited geographic space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:**

 
 
• Population density is a key demographic indicator that reflects the number of people living in a unit area of land.
 
• It is calculated using the formula: **Population Density = Total Population / Land Area**.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census of India:**
 
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of India and provided comprehensive data on population demographics, density, literacy, and other parameters.
 
• It recorded India's population at **1.21 billion**, with a growth rate of 17.7% compared to 2001.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization in Delhi:**
 
 
• Delhi’s rapid urbanization has resulted in high population density, particularly in areas like North East Delhi.
 
• Migrants from different states move to Delhi for job opportunities, education, and improved living standards, contributing to its dense population.
 
 
 
• **Other High-Density Districts:**
 
 
• After North East Delhi, other districts with high population densities include **Central Delhi** and **East Delhi**.
 
• These regions also face challenges such as overcrowding, pressure on infrastructure, and environmental concerns.
